text: Bill begged me. <break time="0.8s" /> With tears in his eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> To ask for fifteen hundred dollars. <break time="0.8s" /> Instead of two thousand. <break time="0.8s" /> Nobody would give up. <break time="0.8s" /> Two thousand dollars. <break time="0.8s" /> For that forty pound wildcat. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> The letter. <break time="0.8s" /> Signed Two Desperate Men. <break time="0.8s" /> Said that the boy was hidden. <break time="0.8s" /> In a place far from Summit. <break time="0.8s" /> It told Dorset. <break time="0.8s" /> To leave the money in a small box. <break time="0.8s" /> At midnight beside a fence post under a tree. <break time="0.8s" /> If he refused. <break time="0.8s" /> The letter warned. <break time="0.8s" /> He would never see his boy again. <break time="0.8s" /> Just as I was leaving. <break time="0.8s" /> The boy made Bill his horse. <break time="0.8s" /> For a ninety mile ride. <break time="0.8s" /> In his Black Scout game. <break time="0.8s" /> I walked to the village of Poplar Cove. <break time="0.8s" /> And mailed the letter. <break time="0.8s" /> At the post office. <break time="0.8s" /> An old man there said that the whole town of Summit was worried. <break time="0.8s" /> About old Dorsets missing boy. <break time="0.8s" /> When I got back to the cave. <break time="0.8s" /> Bill came out alone. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking calm and strangely happy. <break time="0.8s" /> Sam, I have sent the boy home. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> The game is over at last. <break time="0.8s" /> I am sorry, Bill, I said. <break time="0.8s" /> But turn around. <break time="0.8s" /> And look behind you. <break time="0.8s" /> There stood the boy.
